title: Security & Deployment Intake — Redwood / Galileo Pharma

Schedule SE-led technical deep dive (performance + private deployment) week of Feb 2
Provide Dedicated capacity pricing and pilot terms
Share deployment checklist and network/VPC sample configs
action_items: Jordan Ellis - Email SOC2 report, ISO 27001 cert, and network diagrams - due 2026-02-02

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 min | Attendees: Jordan, Priya (Redwood); Emma, Liam, Sofia, Noah (Galileo)

Summary: quick security posture intake to see fit for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Main topics: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC needs, audit logs retention and export, encryption & KMS (BYOK/HSM), data retention for PHI. Customer emphasized regulated clinical research data and legal hold requirements.

Topics: security certificates, key rotation, VPC peering, on-prem bundling, latency vs cost for Dedicated, telemetry and trace redaction.

Action items (recap at end).

Transcript: 
[00:00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood inference, with Priya our solutions engineer. Uh we'll take about 40 minutes, want to understand your security constraints and then propose next steps.
[00:00:14] Emma (Dr): Hi hi, Emma here. We run model ops for Galileo, lots of clinical notes, some PHI, subject to HIPAA plus EU trials so data residency matters.
[00:00:24] Liam (Sec): Liam here. Main ask, we need to know encryption at rest and in transit, KMS options, and auditability. Also team wants SOC2 and ISO evidence.
[00:00:33] Priya (SE): Great, thanks. Quick q: are you evaluating Hosted API first or thinking Dedicated/Private from the start?
[00:00:40] Emma: We're screening all three. Prefer Hosted for dev speed but might need Dedicated or Private for production with PHI, also legal wants to see how SSO and RBAC integrate.
[00:00:48] Jordan: Understood. High level, Redwood offers Hosted API with SOC2 and per-tenant isolation logical, Dedicated with reserved GPU pools and stronger isolation, and Private (VPC/on-prem) where control plane is customer-managed.
[00:00:58] Noah (PlatEng): Quick interruption — what does "Private" actually entail network-wise? VPC peering or full air-gapped on prem?
[00:01:05] Priya: Good question. Private can be a VPC deployment where control plane lives in your cloud region with peering and private endpoints, or an on-prem package for air-gapped. We support BYOK for keys and HSM-backed KMS options.
[00:01:18] Liam: BYOK + HSM is important. We need to ensure key rotation policies run under our KMS and Redwood can't persist plaintext keys.
[00:01:26] Priya: Absolutely — we have a BYOK flow using customer KMS or HSM, and key material is never exported. For Hosted we support envelope encryption with customer keys; Dedicated and Private give more control over key lifecycle and rotation windows.
[00:01:40] Emma: Can you point to the SOC2 scope — is it data plane included? We can't assume all hosted providers include data plane.
[00:01:47] Jordan: Our SOC2 covers both control plane and hosted inference endpoints; we have ISO 27001 in progress for some deployments, and can share the attestation. Priya, I'll drop the documents.
[00:01:56] Priya: Note, some customers ask for an SOC2 bridge letter for specific features — we'll check if we have that for the inference runtime.
[00:02:04] Sofia (Legal): On retention, if we need to hold data for litigation or audits, can logs be exported and preserved immutable?
[00:02:12] Priya: Yes, audit logs are exportable to S3-compatible buckets or SIEMs, with append-only storage recommended. We also support long-term retention policies but retention for PHI often pairs with Private or Dedicated deployments to satisfy legal controls.
[00:02:26] Liam: How granular are audit events? We need per-request traces, token-level usage, user and service principal ids, and model version ids in the logs.
[00:02:35] Priya: Our logs include request metadata (timestamp, model id/version, route, tokens consumed), auth principal, and error traces. We also support request and response sampling to reduce PII in logs; there is configurable verbosity.
[00:02:47] Emma: Sampling worries me — we need for e-discovery to have full records for certain subsets of traffic. Is selective full-logging possible?
[00:02:55] Priya: Yes, you can configure policy to always log specified api-keys or routes. That keeps full records for those flows.
[00:03:02] Noah: For network, does Private offer a customer-managed control plane inside our VPC, or is it a managed control plane that talks via private endpoints?
[00:03:10] Jordan: We have both patterns. Full VPC-hosted control plane deploys into your cloud accounts; managed private is a customer-controlled plane with private connectivity back to Redwood for updates. We can share architecture diagrams.
[00:03:19] Sofia: SSO — we use Okta and require SAML + SCIM for provisioning. Any gaps?
[00:03:25] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, role sync, and groups. RBAC is enforced at the account, team, and route level. We also support attribute-based rules for gating model access.
[00:03:36] Liam: We need separation of duties — devs can call test models but not production models; ops can manage rollouts but not view raw outputs containing PHI. How do you handle output redaction?
[00:03:46] Priya: Redwood Console has role scoping; you can limit access to transcripts. For redaction, we recommend token-level redaction in the ingestion path and specific masking policies. We also support response hooks to strip PII before final storage.
[00:03:58] Emma: Good. About encryption in transit — TLS mutual auth?
[00:04:02] Priya: TLS 1.2+ with mTLS available for Private and Dedicated peering. Hosted supports TLS and private endpoints into your network.
[00:04:09] Jordan: Quick check — do you require audit log immutability via WORM storage?
[00:04:14] Liam: For regulated trials yes, for certain cohorts.
[00:04:17] Priya: We can ship logs to your WORM S3 bucket; Redwood won't be the sole controller for those objects.
[00:04:23] Noah: Any certifications for data processed in EU regions specifically? We have trials in EU.
[00:04:28] Jordan: We have hosted regions in EU; SOC2 is global control, and data residency is configurable by region. For EU-specific compliance we can discuss DPA terms and data processing addendums.
[00:04:38] Sofia: On legal holds — can Redwood suspend deletion policy for a tenant on request?
[00:04:44] Priya: Yes, we can place a retention hold at tenant-level and also export the data. For hosted customers we require a signed request and legal approvals; for Dedicated and Private it's simpler since you control storage.
[00:04:55] Emma: Let's talk about RBAC schema — do you offer custom roles and audit of role changes?
[00:05:01] Priya: Yes, custom roles, audit trail for role assignment and changes, and we export role-change logs as part of the audit bundle.
[00:05:08] Liam: What about secrets management — how are model credentials and tokens stored?
[00:05:12] Priya: Keys are sealed in our secrets store encrypted with a master key; when BYOK is used, the master key is actually your KMS. For Dedicated and Private the secrets live in your KMS/HSM.
[00:05:22] Noah: Are there any limitations on bringing custom models and plugins into Private? We may want to run internal models.
[00:05:28] Jordan: Private supports customer model artifacts; there is a model onboarding process and you can pin versions. We'll work with Research/Applied ML team for compatibility tests.
[00:05:35] Emma: On data retention — what default retention windows do you have for request/response content?
[00:05:40] Priya: Default hosted retention is 30 days for request logs and 90 days for usage metrics; request/response content is configurable and by default is ephemeral unless you enable logging. For PHI customers we typically recommend Dedicated/Private and explicit retention policies.
[00:05:55] Liam: Is there a redaction API or do we need to post-process exported logs?
[00:05:59] Priya: There's a post-processing hook and a managed redaction pipeline we can enable; exports can be sent to your pipeline before persistent storage.
[00:06:06] Sofia: For contractual SLAs, what availability do you offer on Dedicated?
[00:06:10] Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. We can provide the SLA PDF.
[00:06:14] Emma: Regarding forensic needs, can we get a snapshot of the runtime environment and kernel versions used for an inference run? We require that for some audits.
[00:06:21] Priya: We log runtime metadata including model binary hash, runtime version, and kernel selection; that can be included in audit exports.
[00:06:29] Liam: Great. Another point — network egress and how tokens move across regions. Any cross-region replication?
[00:06:36] Jordan: By default we keep data in the region unless you enable cross-region replication. For compliance we recommend single-region deployment for regulated workloads.
[00:06:44] Noah: About tracing — can tracing data be redacted for PII? We don't want traces containing PHI.
[00:06:49] Priya: Traces are configurable; we can scrub payloads and only surface metadata.
[00:06:54] Emma: Do you support hardware-based attestation for models running on GPU hosts?
[00:06:59] Priya: For Dedicated and Private we can provide host attestations and integration with HSMs. For Hosted we have standard host hardening and periodic attestations.
[00:07:07] Liam: Any customer examples with similar PHI constraints?
[00:07:10] Jordan: We have healthcare customers in EU and NA on Dedicated and Private for PHI, can share redacted case studies.
[00:07:15] Sofia: On indemnity and data breach notification timelines, can we get your standard legal template?
[00:07:21] Jordan: Yes, we'll include the security and privacy legal template in the doc pack.
[00:07:25] Priya: Quick technical note — we use KV cache, continuous batching, and a runtime that selects optimized kernels; these internals are configurable for performance and footprint.
[00:07:36] Noah: You said KV cache — that means cache keys may contain prefixes of requests; is anything persisted to disk that could leak PHI?
[00:07:43] Priya: Cache can be in-memory or use encrypted disk storage. For PHI customers we keep cache in encrypted memory-only or provide options to disable caching.
[00:07:52] Emma: Very important.
[00:07:55] Liam: Regarding tokenization metadata — do logs include raw tokens or only counts?
[00:08:00] Priya: By default logs have token counts, not content. If you enable full request/response logging it will include content. We advise masking content unless necessary.
[00:08:10] Emma: Ok. We need to map out who needs what role access; I'll send a matrix.
[00:08:15] Sofia: Also need a copy of the DPA and the data flow diagram.
[00:08:20] Jordan: We'll send DPA, SOC2, ISO progress notes, and a deployment diagram.
[00:08:24] Liam: For pen testing, do you allow third-party pentests on Dedicated/Private?
[00:08:28] Priya: Yes, customers can run pentests on Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we have a coordinated program. We'll provide our pentest contacts and process.
[00:08:36] Emma: About telemetry and metrics — do you sample user prompts for quality monitoring?
[00:08:41] Priya: We do, but sampling is opt-in and configurable; PHI customers usually disable sampling or route it through a redaction pipeline.
[00:08:50] Jordan: We're about a third in time; want to highlight the pilot pattern: many customers start Hosted for dev, then move to Dedicated with a pilot commit and final production on Private if required.
[00:08:59] Emma: That path makes sense. Cost vs latency is key for us.
[00:09:03] Priya: For latency-sensitive workloads we advise Dedicated with provisioned GPUs and local region placement; we can run benchmarks against your typical prompts.
[00:09:12] Noah: Benchmarks — do you provide tooling to run our prompt set and produce token-level latency and cost estimates?
[00:09:18] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes a benchmarking harness and model/quantization recommendations based on your workload. We'll run this in the deep-dive.
[00:09:25] Emma: Any limits on retention for audit logs? We may need 7 years for some records.
[00:09:30] Priya: Long-term retention is possible through exports to your S3/WORM storage; Redwood itself doesn't typically hold seven years of raw traces in Hosted.
[00:09:39] Liam: What about encryption key rotation frequency? We require monthly rotation.
[00:09:44] Priya: With BYOK you control rotation cadence; we can support monthly rotation and show rotation logs in the audit bundle.
[00:09:52] Sofia: Are there controls for developer sandboxing — we don't want test prompts to leak to prod models or to QA teams.
[00:09:58] Priya: Environments and routes can be separated; tokens are scoped to environments and you can enforce network and role restrictions.
[00:10:06] Emma: Great. This is a lot. Can we do a quick recap of items you'll send?
[00:10:11] Jordan: Sure — we'll send SOC2, ISO notes, DPA, KMS architecture, sample RBAC matrix, Dedicated pricing, and a proposed agenda for the SE deep dive.
[00:10:22] Emma: Perfect.
[00:10:24] [..fast-forwarded middle of call.. summaries and clarifications, some interruptions, mis-transcriptions..] 
[00:20:30] Priya: (technical) On audit logs export, we support exporting to Splunk, Datadog, S3, and SIEM via secure transfer. Note that the logs contain auth principal and model id; we can remove payloads from logs via pipeline.
[00:21:05] Liam: Any restrictions on third-party integrators pulling logs? We use an in-house SIEM team.
[00:21:12] Priya: Integrators can pull via secured endpoints with scoped API keys; SCIM and SAML group sync keep provisioning tight.
[00:21:25] Emma: How quickly can you enable a retention hold and export? We might need same-day in an incident.
[00:21:31] Jordan: For Hosted customers it requires a signed request and ops coordination — same-day is possible but depends on request window; Dedicated/Private is quicker since you control storage.
[00:21:45] Noah: Regarding logging volume, do you have cost guidance? Exporting entire request/response content could be huge.
[00:21:52] Priya: We'll provide cost estimates; Redwood Optimize can show token-level costs and recommend sampling or selective full-logging to balance costs.
[00:22:05] Emma: Could you show an example log entry?
[00:22:09] Priya: We'll include a redacted sample with model hash, runtime version, request id, principal id, token count, but not full prompt.
[00:22:20] Liam: For legal compliance we might need proof of deletion as well — a deletion audit. Do you track deletion events?
[00:22:27] Priya: Yes, deletion events are logged and can be included in audit exports; we can show the chain of custody.
[00:22:35] Sofia: Any PII scanning capabilities? We want automated flagging before storing.
[00:22:41] Priya: We have optional PII detectors and hooks to redaction services before storage.
[00:22:48] Emma: How about training/model fine-tuning — do you ever use customer prompts to further train shared models?
[00:22:54] Jordan: We do not use customer prompt data to train shared models unless explicitly opted in; by default data isn't used to train public models and there are contractual guarantees.
[00:23:03] Liam: Good. 
[00:23:07] [00:23:07] Emma: Ok what about SAML metadata exchange — do you support IdP-initiated single sign-on?
[00:23:11] Priya: Yes, both IdP and SP-initiated flows are supported, and SCIM provisioning can be automated.
[00:23:18] Noah: Are session tokens short-lived? We need high rotation for admin sessions.
[00:23:22] Priya: Session TTLs are configurable; admin sessions can be constrained with MFA required. We also support hardware MFA for sensitive roles.
[00:23:31] Emma: Regarding model governance, can you pin model versions per route and do canary rollouts?
[00:23:36] Priya: Yes, rollouts, canary, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies are supported. We log rollout events in the audit log.
[00:23:44] Liam: Forensics again — do you have a packaged audit bundle for a given time window with all relevant logs and configs?
[00:23:49] Jordan: Yes, we can produce an audit bundle containing logs, role change history, model hashes, and runtime metadata for a specified retention window.
[00:23:58] Emma: Excellent. 
[00:24:00] [..call goes into clarifying network diagrams and privacy wording..] 
[00:33:12] Priya: Small note — cache naming in our docs sometimes gets transcribed as "K-V cash" in auto transcripts, it's actually KV cache; that stores intermediate attention states and is controlled by policy. For PHI we suggest disabling or encrypting it in memory-only.
[00:33:28] Liam: We will require memory-only behavior.
[00:33:31] Priya: Noted.
[00:33:34] Sofia: Any minimum contract for Dedicated pilot?
[00:33:37] Jordan: Typical pilot commit is 3 months reserved capacity; we can discuss a shorter eval for proof-of-concept.
[00:33:44] Emma: And billing currency for EU?
[00:33:47] Jordan: We support billing in EUR for EU region customers.
[00:33:51] Noah: For Private on-prem, what's the update path? Do we require scheduled maintenance windows?
[00:33:56] Priya: On-prem package comes with a changelog and scheduled update windows; you control when to apply patches. We also offer managed updates on request.
[00:34:05] Liam: For incident response, do you have a SOC contact list and SLA for breach notifications?
[00:34:10] Jordan: Yes, we'll include our security contact and standard notification timelines in the package.
[00:34:16] Sofia: Final legal q — do you support contractual commitments around data deletion/dpa language for PHI beyond standard DPA?
[00:34:22] Jordan: We can negotiate enhanced DPA terms in enterprise agreements for PHI workloads.
[00:34:27] Emma: Ok that's helpful.
[00:34:30] Jordan: Any final quick questions?
[00:34:33] Liam: Can you show how RBAC maps to audit logs one more time?
[00:34:36] Priya: Sure — role assignment events, permission checks, and resource access attempts are all logged with principal id and outcome. We'll include an example.
[00:34:45] Emma: Thanks. Let's recap next steps.
[00:34:48] Jordan: Recap: we'll send SOC2 and ISO attestation materials, DPA and legal templates, KMS architecture diagrams, sample audit logs and redaction examples, Dedicated pricing and pilot terms, and propose dates for the SE deep dive.
[00:35:03] Sofia: Please include info on legal holds and e-discovery export process.
[00:35:08] Jordan: Will do.
[00:35:10] Emma: Great. Thanks everyone.
[00:35:13] [Call wraps; brief social goodbyes and next steps confirm].

Meeting end. Next steps and action items as above.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., kernel selection referred to as "kernel collection" by auto-transcriber), and speaker labels may shift; please refer to action items for authoritative follow-ups.
